newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees new municipal bond auctions in June.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees new municipal bond auctions in June.

text.p: Russia plans to begin auctions of nine trillion roubles ($1.6 billion) nominal value of municipal-regional bonds on June 19, Ministry of Finance officials said on Monday.

Discount bonds converted from massive unrepaid 1996 federal agricultural credits to the regions, will be auctioned and traded on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX), they told a news conference.
Bonds would be divided by regional issuer, each of which would offer one, two and three year-maturing bonds, they said.

"Different regions will have different discounts," said Deputy Finance Minister Vasily Kovalyov, who heads a working group on the project. Foreigners could buy and trade bonds which would be auctioned up to twice weekly, he said.
Trying to untangle a web of debt between companies, state and regions, and force payment of tax arrears, Russia has been forging ahead recently with initiatives to restructure debt.
The bonds, with 10 percent annual coupons, would represent about 70 regions, Finance Ministry securities department head Bella Zlatkis said last week.
Kovalyov said an additional five trillion roubles of unrepaid 1995 agricultural credits would be converted to bonds if not paid when a deferral comes due on January 1, 1998.

Funds from the bond sales, which Kovalyov said would raise a few trillion roubles, would be used as new agricultural credits to the regions, said ministry securities department deputy director Marina Chekurova.
Auctions would be held where at least two bidders were present and unauctioned paper would be sold on the exchange all at a minimum price set by the ministry, she said.
She said the ministry designed the system so that regions, some of which have their own, generally untransparent municipal bond markets, could issue their own paper on it.

The volume of the market is small in comparison with that for government securities, where the government typically issues 12 trillion roubles of paper a week, and daily trading volume can be around six trillion roubles. ($1=5,770 roubles)
